**_We do not report in detail on Russian war crimes because those activities are well-covered in Western media and do not directly affect the military operations we are assessing and forecasting. We will continue to evaluate and report on the effects of these criminal activities on the Ukrainian military and population and specifically on combat in Ukrainian urban areas. We utterly condemn these Russian violations of the laws of armed conflict, Geneva Conventions, and humanity even though we do not describe them in these reports._**

*   Ukrainian Counteroffensives—Eastern Ukraine
*   Russian Main Effort—Eastern Ukraine (comprised of one subordinate and one supporting effort);
*   Russian Subordinate Main Effort—Capture the entirety of Donetsk Oblast
*   Russian Supporting Effort—Southern Axis
*   Russian Mobilization and Force Generation Efforts
*   Activities in Russian-occupied Areas

**Ukrainian Counteroffensives****(Ukrainian efforts to liberate Russian-occupied territories)**

**Eastern Ukraine:****(Eastern Kharkiv Oblast-Western Luhansk Oblast)**

Ukrainian forces continued to make gains along the Svatove-Kreminna line on January 10. The Ukrainian Center for Defense Strategies confirmed that Ukrainian troops captured Pidkuichansk, 8km northwest of Svatove, on January 8.[[26]](https://www.criticalthreats.org/analysis/russian-offensive-campaign-assessment-january-10-2023#_edn1c27e580fbe82e3a289afba5aab80daa26) Luhansk Oblast Head Serhiy Haidai stated that Russian forces are conducting limited counterattacks near Svatove to regain lost positions in the area.[[27]](https://www.criticalthreats.org/analysis/russian-offensive-campaign-assessment-january-10-2023#_edn1c27e580fbe82e3a289afba5aab80daa27) A Russian milblogger reported that Russian troops attacked near Stelmakhivka, 13km northwest of Svatove.[[28]](https://www.criticalthreats.org/analysis/russian-offensive-campaign-assessment-january-10-2023#_edn1c27e580fbe82e3a289afba5aab80daa28) Geolocated footage shows a Russian tank from the 3rd Motorized Rifle Division of the 20th Combined Arms Army of the Western Military District firing on Ukrainian positions west of Ploshchanka and approximately 17km northwest of Kreminna, indicating that Ukrainian troops have advanced closer to R66 Svatove-Kreminna highway.[[29]](https://www.criticalthreats.org/analysis/russian-offensive-campaign-assessment-january-10-2023#_edn1c27e580fbe82e3a289afba5aab80daa29) A Russian milblogger also remarked that Russian troops attacked Ukrainian positions in the Ploshchanka area, further confirming that Russian troops have lost ground near Kreminna.[[30]](https://www.criticalthreats.org/analysis/russian-offensive-campaign-assessment-january-10-2023#_edn1c27e580fbe82e3a289afba5aab80daa30) The Ukrainian General Staff reported that Ukrainian troops repelled Russian attacks near Chervonopopivka (6km north of Kreminna) and Bilohorivka (10km south of Kreminna).[[31]](https://www.criticalthreats.org/analysis/russian-offensive-campaign-assessment-january-10-2023#_edn1c27e580fbe82e3a289afba5aab80daa31)

![Image 6](https://www.criticalthreats.org/wp-content/uploads/Kharkiv-Battle-Map-Draft-January-102023.png)

**Russian Main Effort—Eastern Ukraine**

**Russian Subordinate Main Effort—Donetsk Oblast****(Russian objective: Capture the entirety of Donetsk Oblast, the claimed territory of Russia’s proxies in Donbas)**

Wagner Group forces made further gains in Soledar on January 10. Spokesperson for the Ukrainian Eastern Group of Forces Serhiy Cherevaty reported that the Wagner Group has concentrated its most capable (likely special operations) forces in Soledar as of January 10.[[32]](https://www.criticalthreats.org/analysis/russian-offensive-campaign-assessment-january-10-2023#_edn1c27e580fbe82e3a289afba5aab80daa32) The Wagner Group likely hopes to build on recent marginal tactical gains by committing more elite assets to the area. Geolocated footage posted on January 9 shows Wagner Group forces fighting in central Soledar.[[33]](https://www.criticalthreats.org/analysis/russian-offensive-campaign-assessment-january-10-2023#_edn1c27e580fbe82e3a289afba5aab80daa33) A Wagner Group-affiliated Telegram group posted additional footage on January 10 of Wagner Group forces near the city administration building in central Soledar and claimed that the Wagner Group is working to consolidate positions in the area.[[34]](https://www.criticalthreats.org/analysis/russian-offensive-campaign-assessment-january-10-2023#_edn1c27e580fbe82e3a289afba5aab80daa34) Certain Russian milbloggers claimed that Wagner Group forces have moved into the western parts of Soledar and that Ukrainian troops have begun withdrawing from the settlement _en masse_.[[35]](https://www.criticalthreats.org/analysis/russian-offensive-campaign-assessment-january-10-2023#_edn1c27e580fbe82e3a289afba5aab80daa35) Wagner Group financier Yevgeny Prigozhin denied these claims and stated that Ukrainian troops are still fighting fiercely for Soledar.[[36]](https://www.criticalthreats.org/analysis/russian-offensive-campaign-assessment-january-10-2023#_edn1c27e580fbe82e3a289afba5aab80daa36) Russian milbloggers also claimed that the Wagner Group is clearing Pidhorodne (just southwest of Soledar) and are moving on Krasna Hora and Paraskoviivka.[[37]](https://www.criticalthreats.org/analysis/russian-offensive-campaign-assessment-january-10-2023#_edn1c27e580fbe82e3a289afba5aab80daa37) The Ukrainian General Staff reported continued fighting in other settlements near Soledar, including Bilohorivka and Pidhorodne.[[38]](https://www.criticalthreats.org/analysis/russian-offensive-campaign-assessment-january-10-2023#_edn1c27e580fbe82e3a289afba5aab80daa38)

Russian forces continued ground attacks in and around Bakhmut on January 10. The Ukrainian General Staff reported that Ukrainian troops repelled attacks on Bakhmut itself and south of Bakhmut near Klishchiivka (7km southwest), Kurdiumivka (12km southwest), and Mayorsk (20km south).[[39]](https://www.criticalthreats.org/analysis/russian-offensive-campaign-assessment-january-10-2023#_edn1c27e580fbe82e3a289afba5aab80daa39) Russian milbloggers claimed that Russian troops are fighting for control of Klishchiivka in order to push north and cut the T0504 Chasiv Yar-Bakhmut highway.[[40]](https://www.criticalthreats.org/analysis/russian-offensive-campaign-assessment-january-10-2023#_edn1c27e580fbe82e3a289afba5aab80daa40) A Russian milblogger claimed that Russian troops have advanced to the northern borders of Opytne (3km south of Bakhmut) and are now on the southern outskirts of Bakhmut.[[41]](https://www.criticalthreats.org/analysis/russian-offensive-campaign-assessment-january-10-2023#_edn1c27e580fbe82e3a289afba5aab80daa41) Russian sources additionally continued to discuss fierce fighting in the industrial zone on the eastern outskirts of Bakhmut.[[42]](https://www.criticalthreats.org/analysis/russian-offensive-campaign-assessment-january-10-2023#_edn1c27e580fbe82e3a289afba5aab80daa42)

Russian forces continued ground attacks along the western outskirts of Donetsk City on January 10. The Ukrainian General Staff stated that Ukrainian forces repelled Russian attacks near Vodiane (on the northwestern outskirts) and Marinka and Pobieda (on the southwestern outskirts).[[43]](https://www.criticalthreats.org/analysis/russian-offensive-campaign-assessment-january-10-2023#_edn1c27e580fbe82e3a289afba5aab80daa43) A Russian milblogger claimed that Russian troops attacked from near Novomykhailivka (just south of Donetsk City) toward Pobieda, about 4km directly south of Marinka.[[44]](https://www.criticalthreats.org/analysis/russian-offensive-campaign-assessment-january-10-2023#_edn1c27e580fbe82e3a289afba5aab80daa44) The Donetsk People’s Republic (DNR) People’s Militia posted footage of the 5th DNR Brigade reportedly striking Ukrainian positions in Marinka.[[45]](https://www.criticalthreats.org/analysis/russian-offensive-campaign-assessment-january-10-2023#_edn1c27e580fbe82e3a289afba5aab80daa45) Russian forces did not conduct any claimed or confirmed ground attacks in western Donetsk or eastern Zaporizhia oblasts and continued routine fire along the entire Avdiivka-Donetsk City and western Donetsk-eastern Zaporizhia oblast frontline.[[46]](https://www.criticalthreats.org/analysis/russian-offensive-campaign-assessment-january-10-2023#_edn1c27e580fbe82e3a289afba5aab80daa46)

![Image 7](https://www.criticalthreats.org/wp-content/uploads/Donetsk-Battle-Map-Draft-January-102023.png)

**Supporting Effort—Southern Axis****(Russian objective: Maintain frontline positions and secure rear areas against Ukrainian strikes)**

Russian and Ukrainian forces continued routine strikes across the Dnipro River in Kherson Oblast on January 10. A Ukrainian source claimed that Ukrainian forces shot down a Russian Ka-52 attack helicopter near Kherson City.[[47]](https://www.criticalthreats.org/analysis/russian-offensive-campaign-assessment-january-10-2023#_edn1c27e580fbe82e3a289afba5aab80daa47) A Russian milblogger claimed that Russian forces struck a 200-person concentration of Ukrainian security personnel in Kherson City and inflicted high casualties.[[48]](https://www.criticalthreats.org/analysis/russian-offensive-campaign-assessment-january-10-2023#_edn1c27e580fbe82e3a289afba5aab80daa48) ISW has not observed visual observation of this claim. ISW previously reported on January 8 that Russian military leadership is attempting to present similar claimed strikes on Ukrainian concentrations areas as "retaliation" for the December 31 Ukrainian strike on Russian positions in Makiivka, Donetsk Oblast, which reportedly killed up to 400 mobilized servicemen.[[49]](https://www.criticalthreats.org/analysis/russian-offensive-campaign-assessment-january-10-2023#_edn1c27e580fbe82e3a289afba5aab80daa49) Russian forces shelled various areas of west (right) bank Kherson Oblast, including the Kherson City area and areas 33km west of Kherson City near Stanislav and Shyroka Balka.[[50]](https://www.criticalthreats.org/analysis/russian-offensive-campaign-assessment-january-10-2023#_edn1c27e580fbe82e3a289afba5aab80daa50) Russian and Ukrainian sources reported that Ukrainian forces struck Tavriisk, Nova Kakhovka, and Skadovsk Raion, Kherson Oblast.[[51]](https://www.criticalthreats.org/analysis/russian-offensive-campaign-assessment-january-10-2023#_edn1c27e580fbe82e3a289afba5aab80daa51)

Ukrainian officials reported that Russian forces continued to focus on holding occupied lines in the Zaporizhia direction on January 10.[[52]](https://www.criticalthreats.org/analysis/russian-offensive-campaign-assessment-january-10-2023#_edn1c27e580fbe82e3a289afba5aab80daa52) Ukrainian Zaporizhia Oblast Head Oleksandr Starukh stated on January 9 that severe winter weather increases the likelihood of intense Russian combat reconnaissance along the Zaporizhia Oblast front line.[[53]](https://www.criticalthreats.org/analysis/russian-offensive-campaign-assessment-january-10-2023#_edn1c27e580fbe82e3a289afba5aab80daa53) Russian forces continued routine fire in Zaporizhia, Mykolaiv, and Dnipropetrovsk oblasts on January 10.[[54]](https://www.criticalthreats.org/analysis/russian-offensive-campaign-assessment-january-10-2023#_edn1c27e580fbe82e3a289afba5aab80daa54) Ukrainian Mykolaiv Oblast Head Vitaly Kim stated on January 10 that Russian forces struck Ochakiv, Mykolaiv Oblast six times within 24 hours, and Spokesperson for Ukraine's Southern Operational Command, Natalya Humenyuk, stated that Russian forces targeted Ochakiv in retaliation for Ukrainian military successes.[[55]](https://www.criticalthreats.org/analysis/russian-offensive-campaign-assessment-january-10-2023#_edn1c27e580fbe82e3a289afba5aab80daa55)

Ukrainian officials reported that Russian forces continue to militarize the Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant (ZNPP). Ukrainian Atomic Energy Regulatory Commission Head Oleh Korkiv stated on January 10 that the Russian military established a military equipment and repair base at the ZNPP amid ongoing negotiations on the demilitarization of the ZNPP.[[56]](https://www.criticalthreats.org/analysis/russian-offensive-campaign-assessment-january-10-2023#_edn1c27e580fbe82e3a289afba5aab80daa56) Korkiv also stated that Russian authorities have tried and failed multiple times to connect the ZNPP to the Russian power grid, and stated he is confident that further attempts will be unsuccessful.[[57]](https://www.criticalthreats.org/analysis/russian-offensive-campaign-assessment-january-10-2023#_edn1c27e580fbe82e3a289afba5aab80daa57) The Head of the Ukrainian Joint Press Center of the Tavrisk Direction Defense Forces, Yevhen Yerin, stated on January 8 that Russian forces continue to store military personnel and equipment at the ZNPP.[[58]](https://www.criticalthreats.org/analysis/russian-offensive-campaign-assessment-january-10-2023#_edn1c27e580fbe82e3a289afba5aab80daa58)

Russian occupation authorities continued efforts to restore the Kerch Strait Bridge. Russian occupation authorities announced on January 10 that Russian authorities laid the first new span of the west (left) road bridge.[[59]](https://www.criticalthreats.org/analysis/russian-offensive-campaign-assessment-january-10-2023#_edn1c27e580fbe82e3a289afba5aab80daa59) Occupation authorities claim that they plan to complete repairs to the road bridge by March 2023.[[60]](https://www.criticalthreats.org/analysis/russian-offensive-campaign-assessment-january-10-2023#_edn1c27e580fbe82e3a289afba5aab80daa60) Russian forces have likely struggled to compensate for their diminished logistics capacity following the Kerch Strait Bridge attack, as ISW has previously reported.[[61]](https://www.criticalthreats.org/analysis/russian-offensive-campaign-assessment-january-10-2023#_edn1c27e580fbe82e3a289afba5aab80daa61)

**Mobilization and Force Generation Efforts****(Russian objective: Expand combat power without conducting general mobilization)**

The Kremin continues to deny that Russian authorities are preparing for another wave of "partial mobilization." Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov denied reports of a new wave of partial mobilization on January 9 and called on Russian citizens to ignore Telegram channels that speculate about new mobilization efforts.[[62]](https://www.criticalthreats.org/analysis/russian-offensive-campaign-assessment-january-10-2023#_edn1c27e580fbe82e3a289afba5aab80daa62) As ISW continues to assess, discussion of a second wave of mobilization is erroneous to some extent because mobilization has never truly ceased and the Kremlin has conducted a greater, ongoing effort to recruit reservists and others into service since before February 2022.[[63]](https://www.criticalthreats.org/analysis/russian-offensive-campaign-assessment-january-10-2023#_edn1c27e580fbe82e3a289afba5aab80daa63)

Russian occupation authorities continue mobilizing Ukrainian citizens in occupied Ukraine. The Luhansk People’s Republic (LNR) People’s Militia posted a video on January 10 of LNR recruiters working with Luhansk Oblast residents who "volunteered" to fight in the Russian military.[[64]](https://www.criticalthreats.org/analysis/russian-offensive-campaign-assessment-january-10-2023#_edn1c27e580fbe82e3a289afba5aab80daa64) The Ukrainian General Staff reported that Russian authorities mobilized 30 people - including four people with disabilities - during a raid in Horlivka, Donetsk Oblast, on January 6, and sent these people to service with a military unit after only two days of training.[[65]](https://www.criticalthreats.org/analysis/russian-offensive-campaign-assessment-january-10-2023#_edn1c27e580fbe82e3a289afba5aab80daa65)

**Activity in Russian-occupied Areas****(Russian objective: consolidate administrative control of and annexed areas; forcibly integrate Ukrainian civilians into Russian sociocultural, economic, military, and governance systems)**

Russian occupation authorities are struggling to contain an effective partisan movement in occupied territories that is likely improving the targeting intelligence of Ukrainian forces. The Ukrainian Resistance Center claimed on January 10 that Ukrainian partisans were responsible for a January 8 explosion at a Russian ammunition depot near the Hidromash factory in Melitopol, Zaporizhia Oblast.[[66]](https://www.criticalthreats.org/analysis/russian-offensive-campaign-assessment-january-10-2023#_edn1c27e580fbe82e3a289afba5aab80daa66) Partisans may have sabotaged the depot or provided intelligence on the location of the ammunition depot to enable Ukrainian strikes.

Russian occupation authorities continue to search for pro-Ukrainian civilians and partisans in occupied parts of Zaporizhia Oblast. Ukrainian Mayor of Melitopol, Ivan Fedorov, reported on January 10 that occupation authorities are conflating pro-Ukraine sentiments with partisan activity and are advertising social media forums for residents to report Ukrainian partisans or anyone with a pro-Ukrainian viewpoint to occupation authorities.[[67]](https://www.criticalthreats.org/analysis/russian-offensive-campaign-assessment-january-10-2023#_edn1c27e580fbe82e3a289afba5aab80daa67) Fedorov reported that occupation officials are encouraging residents to anonymously report their neighbors in exchange for money and are intimidating Ukrainian civilians through "preventative talks" and torture. Fedorov reported that occupation officials who capture pro-Ukraine civilians deport them "outside of the occupied territories," likely to Russia. A senior official within the Zaporizhia Occupation Administration, Vladimir Rogov, announced on January 10 that Russian forces will search garages in Tokmak on January 13 for unspecified "dangerous contents."[[68]](https://www.criticalthreats.org/analysis/russian-offensive-campaign-assessment-january-10-2023#_edn1c27e580fbe82e3a289afba5aab80daa68) Occupation authorities may intend such preemptive announcements to draw out Ukrainian partisans for arrest if Russian intelligence did identify a partisan storage site, but may instead be setting conditions for simple theft via seizures of allegedly suspicious vehicles. Russian occupation authorities have repeatedly stolen cars, appliances, and other valuables belonging to Ukrainian civilians in occupied areas to export and resell them within Russia for personal gain.[[69]](https://www.criticalthreats.org/analysis/russian-offensive-campaign-assessment-january-10-2023#_edn1c27e580fbe82e3a289afba5aab80daa69)

**ISW will continue to report daily observed indicators consistent with the current assessed most dangerous course of action (MDCOA): a renewed invasion of northern Ukraine possibly aimed at Kyiv.**

**_ISW’s December 15 MDCOA warning forecast about a potential Russian offensive against northern Ukraine in winter 2023 remains a worst-case scenario within the forecast cone. ISW currently assesses the risk of a Russian invasion of Ukraine from Belarus as low, but possible, and the risk of Belarusian direct involvement as very low. This new section in the daily update is not in itself a forecast or assessment. It lays out the daily observed indicators we are using to refine our assessments and forecasts, which we expect to update regularly. Our assessment that the MDCOA remains unlikely has not changed. We will update this header if the assessment changes._**

**Observed indicators for the MDCOA in the past 24 hours:**

*   The Ukrainian General Staff deviated from its normal reporting pattern about Russian forces in Belarus and near Ukraine’s northern border on January 10 by excluding its usual statement that Ukraine has not observed Russian forces forming strike groups in Belarus or northern Ukraine.[[70]](https://www.criticalthreats.org/analysis/russian-offensive-campaign-assessment-january-10-2023#_edn1c27e580fbe82e3a289afba5aab80daa70) This is the first time the Ukrainian General Staff has excluded this statement since it reintroduced discussing Russian forces in Belarus on November 20.[[71]](https://www.criticalthreats.org/analysis/russian-offensive-campaign-assessment-january-10-2023#_edn1c27e580fbe82e3a289afba5aab80daa71) This could indicate that the Ukrainian military has observed Russian forces forming strike groups in northern Ukraine. Alternatively, the situation may not have changed, and the Ukrainian General Staff may have left it out of the daily report in an isolated incident. ISW will continue to monitor and assess the language of Ukrainian General Staff reports.

**Observed ambiguous indicators for MDCOA in the past 24 hours:**

*   _Reuters_ reported that Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said that Russia is "gathering forces for another escalation" but did not specify where, when, or how the unspecified escalation could occur.[[72]](https://www.criticalthreats.org/analysis/russian-offensive-campaign-assessment-january-10-2023#_edn1c27e580fbe82e3a289afba5aab80daa72)
*   Russian forces continue to deploy Russian elements to Belarus. Social media footage posted on January 10 reportedly shows likely Russian military equipment, including tube artillery with winter camouflage, on a train in Belarus moving west.[[73]](https://www.criticalthreats.org/analysis/russian-offensive-campaign-assessment-january-10-2023#_edn1c27e580fbe82e3a289afba5aab80daa73) As ISW previously noted, applying winter camouflage to equipment is not wholly necessary for training activity and could indicate preparation for actual winter combat operations.[[74]](https://www.criticalthreats.org/analysis/russian-offensive-campaign-assessment-january-10-2023#_edn1c27e580fbe82e3a289afba5aab80daa74)

**Observed counter-indicators for the MDCOA in the past 24 hours:**

*   Nothing significant to report.

**Volodymyr Oleksandrovych Zelenskyy**[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-4) (born 25 January 1978) is a Ukrainian politician and former entertainer who has served as the sixth [president of Ukraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Ukraine "President of Ukraine") since 2019. He took office five years after the start of the [Russo-Ukrainian war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russo-Ukrainian_war "Russo-Ukrainian war") with [Russia's annexation of Crimea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annexation_of_Crimea_by_the_Russian_Federation "Annexation of Crimea by the Russian Federation") and [invasion of the Donbas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_in_Donbas "War in Donbas"), and has continued to serve during the full-scale [Russian invasion of Ukraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russo-Ukrainian_war_(2022%E2%80%93present) "Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)"), which has been ongoing since February 2022.

Born in [Kryvyi Rih](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kryvyi_Rih "Kryvyi Rih") into a [Russian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_language_in_Ukraine "Russian language in Ukraine")-speaking [Jewish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_the_Jews_in_Ukraine "History of the Jews in Ukraine") family, Zelenskyy obtained a law degree at the city's [Institute of Economics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kryvyi_Rih_Institute_of_Economics "Kryvyi Rih Institute of Economics"), but instead pursued a career in comedy and entertainment. Zelenskyy co-founded the production company [Kvartal 95](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kvartal_95 "Kvartal 95"), which produced films, cartoons, and television shows including the television series _[Servant of the People](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Servant\_of\_the\_People\_(2015\_TV\_series) "Servant of the People (2015 TV series)")_, in which he played a fictional Ukrainian president. The series aired from 2015 to 2019 and was immensely popular. [A political party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Servant_of_the_People "Servant of the People") with the same name as the television show was founded in March 2018 by Zelenskyy and other associates of Kvartal 95. During his campaign in the [2019 presidential election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Ukrainian_presidential_election "2019 Ukrainian presidential election"), Zelenskyy positioned himself as [anti-establishment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-establishment "Anti-establishment") and [anti-corruption](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-corruption "Anti-corruption"), and had already been a frontrunner in [opinion polls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opinion_polling_for_the_2019_Ukrainian_presidential_election "Opinion polling for the 2019 Ukrainian presidential election") months before he declared his candidacy. He won the election with 73.23 percent of the vote in the second round, defeating incumbent president [Petro Poroshenko](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petro_Poroshenko "Petro Poroshenko") in the biggest landslide in the history of [Ukrainian presidential elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ukrainian_presidential_elections "Ukrainian presidential elections"). His party won a landslide victory in [the snap parliamentary election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Ukrainian_parliamentary_election "2019 Ukrainian parliamentary election") held shortly after [his inauguration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inauguration_of_Volodymyr_Zelenskyy "Inauguration of Volodymyr Zelenskyy").

As president, Zelenskyy has been a proponent of [e-government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E-government "E-government"), and of unity between the [Ukrainian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ukrainian_language "Ukrainian language")- and Russian-speaking parts of [the country's population](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demographics_of_Ukraine "Demographics of Ukraine").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-Hosa_2019-5):11–13 He makes extensive use of [social media](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_media_use_in_politics "Social media use in politics").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-Hosa_2019-5):7–10 During the first two years of his presidency, Zelenskyy oversaw some limited progress in tackling [corruption in Ukraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corruption_in_Ukraine "Corruption in Ukraine"),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-6)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-Wilson_2021-7)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-ft_profile-8) the ending of legal immunity for members of parliament (the [Verkhovna Rada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Verkhovna_Rada "Verkhovna Rada")),[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-9) as well as the country's [response to the COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Ukraine "COVID-19 pandemic in Ukraine") and [subsequent economic recession](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_recession "COVID-19 recession").

During his early presidency, Zelenskyy attempted to end the war in Donbas by implementing the [Minsk agreements](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minsk_agreements "Minsk agreements") through the "[Steinmeier formula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steinmeier_formula "Steinmeier formula")", and sought dialogue with Russian president [Vladimir Putin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vladimir_Putin "Vladimir Putin").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-BBC_10_Dec_2019-10)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-Chatham_Lutsevych-11) During 2021, there was a large Russian military buildup on Ukraine's borders and increased attacks by [Russian proxy forces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_separatist_forces_in_Ukraine "Russian separatist forces in Ukraine"), sparking [an international crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prelude_to_the_2022_Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine "Prelude to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine"). Zelenskyy said his military would not respond to provocations.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-Guardian_18_Feb_2022-12) He attempted to calm the Ukrainian people and asked for military support from [NATO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NATO "NATO").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-Fr24_Seibt-13) On 24 February 2022, Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine. Zelenskyy remained in the capital [Kyiv](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyiv "Kyiv") as it came under attack, declining international offers to evacuate him. He declared [martial law across Ukraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martial_law_in_Ukraine "Martial law in Ukraine") and a general mobilisation of the armed forces.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-14)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-15) There have reportedly been numerous [Russian assassination attempts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assassination_attempts_on_Volodymyr_Zelenskyy "Assassination attempts on Volodymyr Zelenskyy") on Zelenskyy since the invasion.

During the [early peace negotiations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peace_negotiations_in_the_Russo-Ukrainian_war_(2022%E2%80%93present)#Early_negotiations_(February%E2%80%93April_2022) "Peace negotiations in the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)"), Zelenskyy demanded a ceasefire and Russian withdrawal, said he was willing to discuss Ukraine becoming a [neutral country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neutral_country "Neutral country") if given "real" security guarantees, and was willing to negotiate the status of Crimea and Donbas. He presented [Ukraine's Peace Formula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ukraine's_Peace_Formula "Ukraine's Peace Formula") in late 2022, and the [Victory Plan for Ukraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victory_Plan_for_Ukraine "Victory Plan for Ukraine") in late 2024. After Russia ["annexed" southeastern Ukraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_annexation_of_Donetsk,_Kherson,_Luhansk_and_Zaporizhzhia_oblasts "Russian annexation of Donetsk, Kherson, Luhansk and Zaporizhzhia oblasts"), Zelenskyy applied for [Ukraine to join NATO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ukraine%E2%80%93NATO_relations "Ukraine–NATO relations"). He has frequently visited frontline and newly liberated areas,[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-BBC_Bakhmut-16)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-BBC_Izyum-17)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-BBC_Kherson-18)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-KI_Kupiansk-19)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-AP_frontline-20)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-UP_Pokrovsk-21) and met with other world leaders, calling on the international community to support Ukraine's resistance, to provide Ukraine with [military aid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_military_aid_to_Ukraine_during_the_Russo-Ukrainian_war "List of military aid to Ukraine during the Russo-Ukrainian war"), and to impose tougher sanctions on Russia to bring an end to its war. As well as visiting Ukrainian troops on the frontlines, Zelenskyy has repeatedly met with other world leaders, calling on the international community to support Ukraine's resistance and its efforts to end Russia's war. Zelenskyy has called for an unconditional ceasefire and negotiations based on a [20-point peace plan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peace_negotiations_in_the_Russo-Ukrainian_war_(2022%E2%80%93present) "Peace negotiations in the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)").

Zelenskyy was named the [_Time_ Person of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_Person_of_the_Year "Time Person of the Year") for 2022.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-Liga2020-22)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-slovoidilo-23)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-up_kuchma-24)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-25) Rating Group polls in 2022 and 2026 have ranked Zelenskyy among the five most outstanding Ukrainians of all time.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-rating_outstanding_2026-26)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-prm_outstanding_2026-27)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-komersant_outstanding_2026-28)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-rating_outstanding-29)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-up_outstanding-30)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-lb_outstanding-31) Zelenskyy's term was originally scheduled to end in May 2024, but the ongoing Russian invasion and the resulting martial law prevents [the regularly scheduled presidential election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Next_Ukrainian_presidential_election "Next Ukrainian presidential election") from being held. He is expected to remain president for the duration of the war.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-32) Due to this extension of his term, Zelenskyy is the [second-longest serving president](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Ukrainian_presidents_by_length_of_tenure "List of Ukrainian presidents by length of tenure") after Kuchma.

## Early life

Volodymyr Oleksandrovych Zelenskyy was born into a [Jewish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_the_Jews_in_Ukraine "History of the Jews in Ukraine") family on 25 January 1978 in [Kryvyi Rih](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kryvyi_Rih "Kryvyi Rih"), an industrial city in [Ukrainian SSR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ukrainian_SSR "Ukrainian SSR"), Soviet Union.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-LIGAZelenskybio-33)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-34)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-nyt1-35) His mother, Rymma Zelenska, is a retired engineer, while his father, [Oleksandr Zelenskyy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oleksandr_Zelenskyy "Oleksandr Zelenskyy") – a professor and [computer scientist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_scientist "Computer scientist") – is the head of the Department of Cybernetics and Computing Hardware at the [Kryvyi Rih State University of Economics and Technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kryvyi_Rih_State_University_of_Economics_and_Technology "Kryvyi Rih State University of Economics and Technology").[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-36)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-37)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-gordon-38) Oleksandr's father, [Semyon Zelenskyy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semyon_Zelenskyy "Semyon Zelenskyy"), served as an [infantryman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infantryman "Infantryman"), reaching the rank of [colonel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polkovnik "Polkovnik") in the [Red Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Army "Red Army") (in the [57th Guards Motor Rifle Division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/57th_Guards_Motor_Rifle_Division "57th Guards Motor Rifle Division")) during the [Second World War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_World_War "Second World War").[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-39)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-DetroitJewishNews_20220228-40)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-41) Semyon's father and three brothers were killed during [the Holocaust](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Holocaust_in_Ukraine "The Holocaust in Ukraine").[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-18Things-42)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-43)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-44)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-afrhometown-45) Zelenskyy said in March 2022 that, during a massacre, both of Semyon's parents were killed after [German troops](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wehrmacht "Wehrmacht") burned their home to the ground.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-46) Oleksandr's mother survived the Second World War after leaving Kryvyi Rih in an evacuation of Jews to [Almaty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaty "Almaty"), Kazakh SSR, and returned to Ukrainian SSR after the war.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-timesofisrael-47)

Before starting [elementary school](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Education_in_Ukraine "Education in Ukraine"), Zelenskyy spent four years in [Erdenet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erdenet "Erdenet"), Mongolia, where Oleksandr worked as a [mining engineer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mining_engineer "Mining engineer") from the mid-1970s to help build a [copper mine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copper_mine "Copper mine"), applying his abilities in computer science to mining.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-48) Zelenskyy grew up speaking [Russian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_language_in_Ukraine "Russian language in Ukraine").[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-DetroitJewishNews_20220228-40)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-49) At the age of 16, he took the [Test of English as a Foreign Language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Test_of_English_as_a_Foreign_Language "Test of English as a Foreign Language") and received an education grant to study in Israel, but Oleksandr did not allow him to go.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-ZQ-50) Zelenskyy later earned a law degree from the [Kryvyi Rih Institute of Economics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kryvyi_Rih_Institute_of_Economics "Kryvyi Rih Institute of Economics"), then a department of [Kyiv National Economic University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyiv_National_Economic_University "Kyiv National Economic University") and now part of [Kryvyi Rih National University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kryvyi_Rih_National_University "Kryvyi Rih National University"), but never worked in the legal field.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-LIGAZelenskybio-33)[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-0396374-zelenskiy-51)

## Entertainment career

### _KVN_ (1995–2003)

At age 17, Zelenskyy joined his local team competing in _[KVN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KVN "KVN")_,[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-LIGAZelenskybio-33) a comedy competition popular across [former Soviet countries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commonwealth_of_Independent_States "Commonwealth of Independent States").[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-Derix-52):15–16 He was soon invited to join another Ukrainian team known as "Zaporizhzhia-Kryvyi Rih-Transit",[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-LIGAZelenskybio-33)[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-kvart-53) where he became dance director and writer in 1995.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-ZelenskyEffect-54):60 The Transit team performed in KVN's Major League and eventually won in 1997[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-kvnru-55) in a tie with Armenian opponents.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-Zygar-56):184

That same year, Zelenskyy created and headed a new team known as Kvartal 95 together with other Transit members, such as [Oleksandr Pikalov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oleksandr_Pikalov "Oleksandr Pikalov") and [Olena Kravets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olena_Kravets "Olena Kravets");[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-LIGAZelenskybio-33)[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-ZelenskyEffect-54):60 this team was named after the [Kvartal 95 neighbourhood in Kryvyi Rih](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/95th_Kvartal,_Kryvyi_Rih "95th Kvartal, Kryvyi Rih") where he had grown up. From 1999 to 2003, Kvartal 95 performed in the highest open Ukrainian league of KVN as well as in the KVN Major League;[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-kvart-53) they were the only Ukrainian team in the Moscow-based highest league of KVN.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-ZelenskyEffect-54):61 The team members lived in Moscow much of the time, without a fixed address and struggling financially;[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-Derix-52):20–21 they constantly toured former Soviet countries.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-LIGAZelenskybio-33)[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-kvart-53)

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b1/%D0%97%D0%B5%D0%BB%D0%B5%D0%BD%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%B8%D0%B9.jpg/250px-%D0%97%D0%B5%D0%BB%D0%B5%D0%BD%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%B8%D0%B9.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:%D0%97%D0%B5%D0%BB%D0%B5%D0%BD%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%B8%D0%B9.jpg)

Zelenskyy in Prague in 2009

Zelenskyy and Kvartal 95 left KVN in 2003, after prolonged tension with KVN's Russian management over money, political censorship,[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-Derix-52):34 and other disputes.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-Zygar-56):214 Finally, Zelenskyy declined a highly paid job offer from KVN management that would have required him to abandon Kvartal 95, choosing instead to stay with his team and return to Ukraine.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-LIGAZelenskybio-33)[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-arte-57)[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-showman-58):50[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-ZelenskyEffect-54):107[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-Zygar-56):214 An incident where a Russian KVN producer used an antisemitic insult against Zelenskyy on stage also contributed to the split.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-showman-58):50[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-arte-57):45:54

### Kvartal 95 Studio (2003–2019)

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1e/Zelenskyy_and_Koshovy_Teletriumph.jpg/250px-Zelenskyy_and_Koshovy_Teletriumph.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Zelenskyy_and_Koshovy_Teletriumph.jpg)

Zelenskyy (left) and [Yevhen Koshovyi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yevhen_Koshovyi "Yevhen Koshovyi") (right) co-hosting the opening portion of [Teletriumph 2011](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teletriumph_Awards "Teletriumph Awards"), the national television awards of Ukraine. [Kvartal 95](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kvartal_95_Studio "Kvartal 95 Studio") wrote the script and hosted the 2011 ceremony.

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/63/KVARTAL_95_Vadim_Chuprina.jpg/250px-KVARTAL_95_Vadim_Chuprina.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:KVARTAL_95_Vadim_Chuprina.jpg)

Zelenskyy (centre) performing with Kvartal 95 in 2018

After leaving KVN, the Kvartal 95 team moved to [Kyiv](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyiv "Kyiv"),[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-Zygar-56):214 where Zelenskyy and the brothers Borys and [Serhiy Shefir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serhiy_Shefir "Serhiy Shefir") – who had been members of the Transit KVN team – founded the [Kvartal 95 Studio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kvartal_95_Studio "Kvartal 95 Studio") company in September 2003.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-Derix-52):36–37 That same year, Kvartal 95 started producing TV shows for the Ukrainian TV channel [1+1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1+1_(TV_channel) "1+1 (TV channel)"). In 2005, Kvartal 95 moved to the Ukrainian TV channel [Inter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inter_(TV_channel) "Inter (TV channel)"),[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-LIGAZelenskybio-33)[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-Derix-52):43 where they launched the _[Evening Kvartal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evening\_Kvartal?action=edit&redlink=1 "Evening Kvartal (page does not exist)")[[uk](https://uk.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%92%D0%B5%D1%87%D1%96%D1%80%D0%BD%D1%96%D0%B9%20%D0%9A%D0%B2%D0%B0%D1%80%D1%82%D0%B0%D0%BB "uk:Вечірній Квартал")]_ comedy show the same year.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-showman-58):54[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-Derix-52):42[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-Zygar-56):248 This show's format was "theatre-style" with a mixture of [skits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skit_comedy "Skit comedy"), appearances by celebrities, and [stand-up comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stand-up_comedy "Stand-up comedy");[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-Derix-52):42–43 it included sketches on everyday life as well as political satire.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-Derix-52):42–47[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-ZelenskyEffect-54):136–138 _Evening Kvartal_ was the most popular comedy television show in Ukraine in the 2000s,[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-Zygar-56):248 and over 85% of Ukrainians reported they had seen it by the time Zelenskyy became president in 2019.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-ZelenskyEffect-54):137 Kvartal 95 returned to 1+1 in 2012.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-ZelenskyEffect-54):110

Kvartal 95 has been described by biographers as an "empire", a "comedy factory",[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-Derix-52):51 and the "most successful production studio" in Ukraine.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-showman-58):59 Apart from _Evening Kvartal_, the company also launched other show formats including Zelenskyy, such as [Chisto News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chisto_News?action=edit&redlink=1 "Chisto News (page does not exist)"), [League of Laughter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Laughter?action=edit&redlink=1 "League of Laughter (page does not exist)")[[uk](https://uk.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%9B%D1%96%D0%B3%D0%B0%20%D1%81%D0%BC%D1%96%D1%85%D1%83 "uk:Ліга сміху")], and [Make the Comedian Laugh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Make_the_Comedian_Laugh?action=edit&redlink=1 "Make the Comedian Laugh (page does not exist)")[[uk](https://uk.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%A0%D0%BE%D0%B7%D1%81%D0%BC%D1%96%D1%88%D0%B8%20%D0%BA%D0%BE%D0%BC%D1%96%D0%BA%D0%B0 "uk:Розсміши коміка")]. By 2013, the third – a format in which contestants attempted to make comedians laugh – had been sold into China, Italy, and Finland,[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-comedianlaugh-59)[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-detector_laugh-60) and Zelenskyy said in 2018 that he received royalties from 21 countries for the show.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-ZQ-50)

As Zelenskyy's and Kvartal 95's popularity grew, he and they were frequently invited to host or perform at corporate and private events.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-Zygar-56):270 Zelenskyy said in 2018 that he had performed in front of numerous presidents of post-Soviet countries,[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-ZelenskyEffect-54):109 including his own predecessors in office, as well as then-Russian president [Dmitry Medvedev](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dmitry_Medvedev "Dmitry Medvedev").[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-Zygar-56):270[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-ZQ-50)

In 2006, Zelenskyy won the first season of [Ukraine's _Dancing with the Stars_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dancing_with_the_Stars_(Ukraine) "Dancing with the Stars (Ukraine)").[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-Zygar-56):261

Apart from comedy, Zelenskyy's film and television career included acting, scriptwriting, direction, and production. In 2008, he began to co-produce the [sitcom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sitcom "Sitcom")_[Svaty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Svaty "Svaty")_ ("The In-Laws"), which was highly popular in Ukraine and Russia[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-Derix-52):81 and was nominated for the Most Popular Sitcom award at the [Festival de Television de Monte-Carlo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Festival_de_Television_de_Monte-Carlo "Festival de Television de Monte-Carlo").[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-Derix-52):50 The same year, he starred in the romantic comedy _[Love in the Big City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Love\_in\_the\_Big\_City\_(2009\_film) "Love in the Big City (2009 film)")_,[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-LIGAZelenskybio-33) and subsequently in its [2010](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Love_in_the_Big_City_2 "Love in the Big City 2") and [2014](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Love_in_the_Big_City_3 "Love in the Big City 3") sequels; he was also co-writer of the second movie[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-bigcity2-61) and co-producer of the third.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-bigcity3-62) In 2011, he co-wrote, co-produced, and played the male protagonist in the film _[Office Romance. Our Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Office\_Romance.\_Our\_Time "Office Romance. Our Time")_.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-officeromance-63) In 2012, he co-produced _[Rzhevsky Versus Napoleon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rzhevsky\_Versus\_Napoleon "Rzhevsky Versus Napoleon")_[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-napoleon-64) and played the role of Napoleon.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-LIGAZelenskybio-33) Zelenskyy also co-wrote, co-produced, and played the male lead in the 2012 romantic comedy _[8 First Dates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/8\_First\_Dates "8 First Dates")_ and its sequels _[8 Best Dates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/8\_Best\_Dates "8 Best Dates")_ (2012) and _[8 New Dates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/8\_New\_Dates "8 New Dates")_ (2014).[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-LIGAZelenskybio-33)[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-8firstdates-65)[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-8bestdates-66)[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-8newdates-67) He also co-wrote, co-produced, and co-directed the 2018 romantic comedy _[Me. You. He. She](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Me.\_You.\_He.\_She "Me. You. He. She")_, and played the male protagonist.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-youheshe-68)

Zelenskyy also recorded the voice of [Paddington Bear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paddington_Bear "Paddington Bear") in the Ukrainian [dub](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dubbing "Dubbing") of _[Paddington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paddington\_(film) "Paddington (film)")_ (2014) and _[Paddington 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paddington\_2 "Paddington 2")_ (2017), and the voice of Red in the Ukrainian dub of _[The Angry Birds Movie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Angry\_Birds\_Movie "The Angry Birds Movie")_.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-suspilne_dubs-69)

Zelenskyy was also popular in Russia before 2014.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-lemonde_russia-70)[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-Derix-52):51 In 2011, he presented [Russia's _X Factor_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faktor_A "Faktor A") with [Filipp Kirkorov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filipp_Kirkorov "Filipp Kirkorov") and [Alla Pugacheva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alla_Pugacheva "Alla Pugacheva").[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-Derix-52):51 In 2013, he presented the New Year's Eve show on the [Russia-1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russia-1 "Russia-1") channel with Russian comedian [Maxim Galkin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maxim_Galkin "Maxim Galkin").[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-lemonde_russia-70) After Russia's [2014 annexation of Crimea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Russian_annexation_of_Crimea "2014 Russian annexation of Crimea"), Kvartal 95 closed its office in Moscow and began shutting down business ties with Russia; Zelenskyy himself stopped working in Russia by the end of 2014.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-showman-58):106–110 By Zelenskyy's estimation, the decision to separate from the Russian market reduced Kvartal 95's average revenue per hour of TV programming from $200,000 to $30,000.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-ZQ-50)[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-showman-58):106–110

Zelenskyy (centre) with Kvartal 95 visiting wounded Ukrainian soldiers in [Odesa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Odesa "Odesa") in 2016

From 2014, Kvartal 95 also began visiting the war zone to perform for Ukrainian soldiers at the front in the [war in Donbas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_in_Donbas "War in Donbas").[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-Derix-52):70–71[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-showman-58):106–110[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-arte-57)[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-ZelenskyEffect-54):246 After Ukrainian media reported that Kvartal 95 had donated [₴](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ukrainian_hryvnia "Ukrainian hryvnia")1 million to the [Ukrainian army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ukrainian_Ground_Forces "Ukrainian Ground Forces") after the start of the [Russo-Ukrainian war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russo-Ukrainian_war "Russo-Ukrainian war"), some Russian politicians and artists petitioned for a ban on Zelenskyy's works in Russia.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-Zelensky1509516953-71)[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-72)

In August 2014, Zelenskyy spoke out against the intention of the [Ukrainian Ministry of Culture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Culture_(Ukraine) "Ministry of Culture (Ukraine)") to ban Russian artists from Ukraine.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-sevas.com358742-73) Since 2015, Ukraine has blacklisted some Russian artists and media deemed part of "information warfare", such as for "anti-Ukrainian rhetoric" or supporting the annexation of Crimea, and barred them from entering Ukraine.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-Zelensky33863697-74) In 2018, Zelenskyy's _Love in the Big City 2_ was banned in Ukraine[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-75) as it included a blacklisted Russian actor.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-bigcity2banned-76) Similarly, the sitcom _Svaty_ co-produced by Zelenskyy was banned in Ukraine in 2017,[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-77) after a Russian lead actor was blacklisted due to allegedly visiting occupied Crimea and supporting the annexation;[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-Derix-52):81 however, it was unbanned in March 2019.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-78)

In 2015, Zelenskyy began to co-produce and star in the television series _[Servant of the People](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Servant\_of\_the\_People\_(2015\_TV\_series) "Servant of the People (2015 TV series)")_, where he played the role of the president of Ukraine.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-0396374-zelenskiy-51)[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-sotp-79) In the series, Zelenskyy's character was a high-school history teacher in his 30s who won the presidential election after a [viral video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viral_video "Viral video") showed him ranting against government [corruption in Ukraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corruption_in_Ukraine "Corruption in Ukraine"). The show ran for three seasons until Zelenskyy's own election as president.

In 2016, while he was the artistic director of Kvartal 95, Zelenskyy co-presented the [Teletriumph Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teletriumph_Awards "Teletriumph Awards"), the national television awards of Ukraine, alongside [Masha Efrosynina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masha_Efrosynina "Masha Efrosynina").[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-:9-80)[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-:11-81) Teletriumph 2016 was held at [Freedom Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freedom_Hall_(Kyiv)?action=edit&redlink=1 "Freedom Hall (Kyiv) (page does not exist)") and was not televised.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-:11-81)[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-:9-80) He also had to leave the stage to accept his own award that night.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-:9-80) However, the television channel that Kvartal 95 had been associated with, Inter, and their parent company Inter Media Group, boycotted the event and did not participate in the nomination process due to disputes within the Ukrainian television industry and the awards organisers.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-:9-80) Zelenskyy reportedly delivered a biting punchline about the boycott.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-:9-80) The president of Inter Media Group then circulated a press release in response.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-82)

Zelenskyy worked mostly in Russian-language productions. The romantic comedy _[Me. You. He. She](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Me.\_You.\_He.\_She "Me. You. He. She")_, released in Ukraine in December 2018, was his first acting role in the Ukrainian language.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-83)[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-84) The first version of the script was written in Ukrainian but was translated into Russian for the Lithuanian actress [Agnė Grudytė](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agn%C4%97_Grudyt%C4%97 "Agnė Grudytė"). Later, the movie was [dubbed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dubbing_(filmmaking)#Ukraine "Dubbing (filmmaking)") into Ukrainian.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-85)

### Inter general producer (2010–2012)

Zelenskyy was a member of the board and the general producer of the TV channel Inter from 2010 to 2012,[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-0396374-zelenskiy-51) where he created 30 new formats.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-Derix-52):51 Later in 2018, Zelenskyy said that [then-President Yanukovych](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viktor_Yanukovych "Viktor Yanukovych") had offered him US$100 million for political control of Kvartal 95's programmes after he became general producer of Inter, but Zelenskyy refused.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-Derix-52):54[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-ZelenskyEffect-54):109–110[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-ZQ-50)

## 2019 presidential election

Main article: [2019 Ukrainian presidential election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Ukrainian_presidential_election "2019 Ukrainian presidential election")

[![Image 13](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/05/Debates_of_Petro_Poroshenko_and_Vladimir_Zelensky_%282019-04-19%29_02.jpg/250px-Debates_of_Petro_Poroshenko_and_Vladimir_Zelensky_%282019-04-19%29_02.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Debates_of_Petro_Poroshenko_and_Vladimir_Zelensky_(2019-04-19)_02.jpg)

Zelenskyy and then-president of Ukraine [Petro Poroshenko](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petro_Poroshenko "Petro Poroshenko"), April 2019

In March 2018, members of Zelenskyy's production company [Kvartal 95](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kvartal_95_Studio "Kvartal 95 Studio") registered a new political party called _[Servant of the People](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Servant\_of\_the\_People\_(political\_party) "Servant of the People (political party)")_ – the same name as the television programme in which Zelenskyy had played the President of Ukraine for the previous three years.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-SPppno31217bb-86)[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-up7196270Z-87) Although Zelenskyy denied any immediate plans to enter politics and said he had registered the party name only to prevent it being appropriated by others,[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-:6-88) there was widespread speculation that he was planning to run. As early as October 2018, three months before his campaign announcement and six months before the presidential election, he was already a frontrunner in opinion polls.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-89)[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-up7196270Z-87) After months of ambiguous statements,[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-:6-88)[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-up7196270Z-87) on 31 December, less than four months from the election, Zelenskyy announced his candidacy for president of Ukraine on the New Year's Eve evening show on the TV channel 1+1.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-ReutersScrutiny-90) His announcement aired during the traditional New Year's Eve address of incumbent president [Petro Poroshenko](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petro_Poroshenko "Petro Poroshenko") on the same channel,[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-ReutersScrutiny-90) which was only played after Zelenskyy's announcement; Zelenskyy said this was unintentional and attributed it to a technical glitch.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-91)

Zelenskyy's presidential campaign against Poroshenko was almost entirely virtual.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-zelensky-190416154745843-92)[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-93) He did not release a detailed policy platform[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-47654242_UkraineKvartal_95-94) and his engagement with mainstream media was minimal;[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-zelensky-190416154745843-92)[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-96) he instead reached out to the electorate via social media channels and [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube") clips.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-zelensky-190416154745843-92) In place of traditional campaign rallies, he conducted [stand-up comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stand-up_comedy "Stand-up comedy") routines across Ukraine with his production company Kvartal 95.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-97)[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-98) On 16 April 2019, a few days before the second round of the election, 20 Ukrainian news outlets called on Zelenskyy to "stop avoiding journalists".[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-zelensky-190416154745843-92) Zelenskyy stated that he was not hiding from journalists but that he did not want to go to talk shows where "people of the old power" were "just doing [PR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_relations "Public relations")" and that he did not have time to satisfy all interview requests.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-99)

The third season of _[Servant of the People](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Servant\_of\_the\_People\_(2015\_TV\_series) "Servant of the People (2015 TV series)")_ started and ended during the 2019 campaign.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-ZelenskyEffect-54):160

Zelenskyy styled himself as an [anti-establishment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-establishment "Anti-establishment"), anti-corruption figure, and said he wished to restore trust in politicians, "to bring professional, decent people to power" and to "change the mood and timbre of the political establishment".[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-SPppno31217bb-86)[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-up7196270Z-87)[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-lection2019555634-100)[Atlantic Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_Council "Atlantic Council") member [Anders Aslund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anders_Aslund "Anders Aslund") said Zelenskyy was not a [populist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Populism "Populism");[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-47654242_UkraineKvartal_95-94) however, other scholars have analysed Zelenskyy's politics in the framework of populism. For instance, political scientist Volodymyr Kulyk described Zelenskyy as practising "inclusionary" populism that claims to defend "the people" against "the elite" while defining "the people" in a way inclusive of all ethnic, linguistic, religious, and other groups.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-Kulyk-101) Scholar Kostiantyn Yanchenko described Zelenskyy's campaign as characterised by "populist [hyperreality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyperreality "Hyperreality")" constructed by the Servant of the People series and Zelenskyy's other comedy shows,[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-hyperreality-102) and argued along with fellow scholar Mattia Zulianello that Zelenskyy and his party were examples of "valence populism" focused on "non-positional topics, such as anti-corruption appeals, political transparency and moral integrity", rather than "economic and socio-cultural issues".[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-valence-103)

Before the elections, Zelenskyy presented a team that included former finance minister [Oleksandr Danylyuk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oleksandr_Danylyuk "Oleksandr Danylyuk") and others.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-104)[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-7212658/_Zelensky-95) During the campaign, concerns were raised over his links to the oligarch [Ihor Kolomoyskyi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ihor_Kolomoyskyi "Ihor Kolomoyskyi"),[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-105) a billionaire businessman who had gained control of the [1+1 Media Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1+1_Media_Group "1+1 Media Group") in 2010. The group operates eight Ukrainian TV channels and broadcast _Servant of the People_ from 2015 to 2019.

Poroshenko and his supporters argued that Zelenskyy's victory would benefit Russia.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-106)[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-107)[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-108)[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-slate-109) On 19 April 2019 at [Olimpiyskiy National Sports Complex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olimpiyskiy_National_Sports_Complex "Olimpiyskiy National Sports Complex") presidential debates were held in the form of a show.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-hroma190419-110)[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-111)[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-112) In his introductory speech, Zelenskyy acknowledged that in 2014 he voted for Poroshenko, but "I was mistaken. We were mistaken. We voted for one Poroshenko, but received another. The first appears when there are video cameras, the other Petro sends [Medvedchuk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viktor_Medvedchuk "Viktor Medvedchuk") privietiki (greetings) to Moscow."[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-hroma190419-110) Although Zelenskyy initially said he would serve only a single term, he walked back this promise in May 2021, saying he had not yet made up his mind.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-7294216Zelensky-113)

Zelenskyy stated that as president he would develop the [economy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economy_of_Ukraine "Economy of Ukraine") and attract investment to Ukraine through "a restart of the [judicial system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judiciary_of_Ukraine "Judiciary of Ukraine")" and restoring confidence in the state.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-7210004/_Zelensky-114) He also proposed a tax amnesty and a 5-per-cent [flat tax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flat_tax "Flat tax") for big business which could be increased "in dialogue with them and if everyone agrees".[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-7210004/_Zelensky-114) According to Zelenskyy, if people would notice that his new government "works honestly from the first day", they would start paying their taxes.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-7210004/_Zelensky-114)

Zelenskyy achieved a plurality of the electorate (30%) in the first round of elections on 31 March 2019.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-CVKResults1stRound-115) In the second round, on 21 April 2019, he received 73 percent of the vote to Poroshenko's 25 percent in the biggest landslide victory in Ukrainian presidential elections[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-slovoidilo-23) and was elected President of Ukraine.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-116)[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-117) Polish president [Andrzej Duda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrzej_Duda "Andrzej Duda") was one of the first European leaders to congratulate Zelenskyy.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy#cite_note-118) French president [Emmanuel Macron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emmanuel_Macron "Emmanue
